title: AI Agent Task Assignment
riido_task: RIID-4720 [Contracts] AI Agent task participant assignment
summary: Task participant AI Agent assignment semantics are generated from API policy, schema, DSL, IR, and OpenAPI fixtures.
invariants: assignable agents include viewer-owned agents and other users' public agents only.
owned agents appear first, display names order inside each group, and equal names are tied by agent_id.
generated assignment requests carry agent_id and optional request_id/instruction; task_id and workspace_id come from URL paths.
projects, milestones, intakes and AI property filler have no generated AI Agent assignment operations; structured Agent mentions on task/subtask comments may request assignment.
participant DELETE accepts an optional assignment_id removal guard and reason; ID-less and body-less path-Agent removal remain supported.
participant removal cancels all observed active executions for the task Agent and preserves terminal results and failure diagnostics.
a new execution before removal commit returns 409 and preserves membership; this mutation scenario belongs to every participant DELETE operation.
thread and history collections require assigned_agent_ids, including an empty array when no persistent memberships exist; execution history does not infer current membership.

loop.observation: Participant dropdown ordering and assignment target scope lived in long policy prose while DSL scenarios already defined assignable, assign, unassign, and v2 agent-assignment routes.
loop.hypothesis: A focused verifier can make task participant assignment drift observable and prevent downstream repos from adding hidden team/API-key assignment inputs.
loop.execute: Verify assignment operations, request/response schemas, policy anchors, forbidden request fields, non-target path absence, DSL/IR tuple parity, and OpenAPI projection.
loop.evaluate: CI fails when assignment operations, schema fields, participant ordering anchors, generated reader, or task-scope boundaries drift.
loop.retrospective: Future assignment surfaces should update API policy/schema fixtures and this manifest before reader text changes.
